analysis:
Examined the doc-only change in docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3 and the `stop` row at ~2126, plus the large head-text excerpts of Qwen TP media, native context, cluster capability and assistant sections). Nothing in those excerpts changes controls: they describe existing cluster/TP behavior, memory admission and sealed collective use, and make no new capability or trust claims. No threat-model entry is invalidated.

The only code change is provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift. It threads an optional `stopStringScope` (CBv2StopStringScope?, default nil) through two initializer/function signatures (lines ~15, 32, 64) and passes it to `matchedStopSequence(candidates:generatedTokens:scope:)` at ~159-160. This only affects which stop sequence is reported for usage signalling (`usageSignal.record`), after the stop reason is already decided. The effect is limited to out-of-band usage detail and does not touch encryption, attestation, auth, or the prompt/completion data path (A-001, TB-002, T-008). A wrong or nil scope would at worst misreport the matched stop sequence, not leak plaintext. I do not see a security regression.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moved from 7933a0fa to 7f00abc4. The pointed-to content is not supplied, so its effect on TB-007 (inference engine, KV/prefix cache T-041, T-028) cannot be assessed. Remaining integration question: review the submodule diff for changes to memory handling, prefix-cache scoping or stop-string handling. The `matchedStopSequence` overload accepting `scope:` is not in the supplied evidence (it is assumed to be in the unchanged EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift), so I could not verify it exists or how it behaves. I did not find the reasoning/tool-call exclusion semantics themselves to be security-relevant.
